item.text: I’m reviewing the current sorter shape before the next change. The last refactor split responsibilities, so I’m targeting the remaining low-level index bookkeeping inside merge operations now.
I’m replacing the raw `leftIndex` / `rightIndex` bookkeeping with a tiny range cursor abstraction. That keeps the merge logic centered on comparisons and copying, instead of open-coded pointer math.
The merge step now uses explicit run cursors instead of scattered index variables. I’m compiling and running again, then I’ll pull the final line references.

I refactored the merge logic in [merge_sort.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/009_merge_sort/merge_sort.java:1) to replace raw index bookkeeping with a small `Run` cursor abstraction. `mergeRange(...)` at [lines 45-60](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/009_merge_sort/merge_sort.java:45) now operates on `left` and `right` runs, using `peek()` and `take()` instead of manually reading and advancing separate indices.

I also updated `copyRemaining(...)` at [lines 62-66](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/009_merge_sort/merge_sort.java:62) to accept a `Run`, and added the `Run` helper itself at [lines 90-116](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/009_merge_sort/merge_sort.java:90). That makes the merge step more declarative and reduces low-level pointer math in the main algorithm.
